title: Nine checks on grant routing and disclosure
question: What additional relationships disappear when each filer is reviewed on its own?
finding: The same-period checks identified 11 reciprocal pair-periods, 5 four-organization circuit-periods and 114 origin/destination pairs with multiple intermediaries across the periods reviewed.
how: Use the latest Form 990 per filer and match the full start and end dates. Sum positive Schedule I cash amounts by directed EIN pair. A pair-period is one pair observed during one tax period. For the missing-data and self-EIN checks, count grant entries before filtering.
limits: These are grant structures and reporting gaps. Their occurrence does not establish the order of payments, a hidden beneficiary or an improper use of City funds. Inspect the underlying project agreements and bank or ledger dates. Examples identify the first filer’s archived return. Schedule I, Part II requires an itemized recipient entry when a domestic organization or government receives more than $5,000 in total grants or assistance from the filer during the tax year. Smaller grants may be absent. Under the IRS instructions, an accrual-basis filer following FASB ASC 958 reports the present value of a grant payable in future years. An amount in the cash-grant column therefore does not establish a transfer date.

rows.question: Did any grant row name the filer’s own EIN?
rows.unit: Individual positive cash-grant entries. Check transcription and related-organization disclosures.

rows.question: How many reported grants could hide a connection because the recipient EIN is missing or malformed?
rows.unit: Positive cash-grant rows with no usable nine-digit recipient EIN. These are excluded from the network.

rows.question: Do two filers report grants to each other in the same exact tax period?
rows.unit: Unordered pairs per period. Amounts and purposes can differ.

rows.question: Did reciprocal grants total exactly the same dollar amount?
rows.unit: Unordered pairs per period with equal annual totals. Annual totals can combine multiple payments.

rows.question: Did reciprocal grants describe at least one purpose in the same words?
rows.unit: Exact matching nonblank purpose after case and whitespace normalization. Standard grant language can recur.

rows.question: Which three-party circuits recur across tax periods?
rows.unit: Distinct directed groups found in at least two exact reporting periods.

rows.question: Do four distinct filers form a directed circuit in one tax period?
rows.unit: Unique directed four-organization circuits per period. Multiple cycles can share grants.

rows.question: Did a payer report separate purpose descriptions for grants to the same recipient?
rows.unit: Directed EIN pairs per period with at least two different purpose descriptions. This can distinguish separate projects.

rows.question: Did two of a grantor’s recipients also report grants to the same downstream organization?
rows.unit: Distinct origin and destination pairs per period with at least two different intermediaries. Every leg has an EIN.

sources.t: IRS, 2023 Schedule I and instructions, Part II (page 3)
IRS, Schedule I instructions for tax years 2024 onward, Part II
